results.summary: This design implements the wolf, goat and cabbage river crossing puzzle as a combinational logic block. Four input pins represent the positions of the farmer, wolf, goat and cabbage, and the outputs drive the segments of a 7-segment display to indicate a win, a loss, or which river bank has an unattended situation. The game is played interactively by setting the input pins to represent the positions of the four characters. The design is built with Wokwi and is intended for educational purposes.

This design implements a cryptographic hash function with a focus on side-channel resistance. It takes a clock and reset on its inputs and drives the seven segments of a display on its outputs, presumably to show internal state or a result. The design is built with Wokwi and is intended for educational purposes. The documentation is minimal and does not describe the internal state encoding or the exact character sequence timing.

This design is an 8x8 bit serial programmable, addressable and playable memory. It uses a shift register to store data and can drive an LED matrix to display the stored pattern. The design is built with Wokwi and includes a UART interface for programming. It is intended for educational purposes.

This design contains free-running oscillators built from combinational loops with dividers, intended to compare simulation against silicon and to provide a true random number source. It is a process and simulation-verification experiment rather than a functional application. The design includes a ring oscillator, a true random number generator, and a clock divider. It is built with Wokwi.

This design is a counter with a 7-segment display output, built with Wokwi. It is intended for educational purposes and demonstrates a finite state machine. The design uses a clock input and drives the seven segments of a display. The documentation is minimal but sufficient to understand the configuration options.

This design implements a logic gate circuit with a 7-segment display output, built with Wokwi. It is intended for educational purposes and demonstrates basic logic operations. The design uses button inputs and drives the seven segments of a display. The documentation is minimal but sufficient to understand the configuration options.

This design generates LED patterns using a shift register and a clock divider, built with Wokwi. It is intended for educational purposes and demonstrates sequential logic. The design uses a clock input and drives LEDs on its outputs. The documentation is minimal but sufficient to understand the configuration options.

This design is a silicon implementation of a simple optical computation. It uses a photodiode interface to sense light and performs a logic operation based on the input. The design is built with Wokwi and is intended for educational purposes. The documentation is minimal but sufficient to understand the configuration options.

This design implements a flip-flop and logic gate circuit, built with Wokwi. It is intended for educational purposes and demonstrates basic sequential logic. The design uses a clock input and drives outputs based on the logic. The documentation is minimal but sufficient to understand the configuration options.

This design is a simple educational project built with Wokwi. It demonstrates basic digital logic concepts and is intended for learning purposes. The design uses a clock input and drives outputs based on the logic. The documentation is minimal but sufficient to understand the configuration options.
